title: Tenant-aware batching policy compiler with canaryed safe-rollbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a policy compiler and recommendation engine that produces per-tenant and per-route batching/caching configs (batch sizes, KV prefetch heuristics, prefix cache eligibility) and deploys them via a canaryed, safe-rollback flow. The compiler should accept segmentation rules (tenant groups, feature flags, SLA tiers), allowlist/denylist overrides for routes, and output deterministic, auditable config bundles that the runtime can apply with minimal downtime.

Success metrics: 1) 8-12% net token-cost reduction on targeted tenants within 2 weeks of rollout; 2) no >5% latency regressions on P95 across canary cohorts; 3) zero customer-impact incidents caused by misapplied policies.

Scope:
- Input: customer profile (tier, historical seq-length distribution, qps), route metadata (model, endpoint, function hints), and ops constraints (allowed quantization, prefetch memory budgets).
- Output: policy bundles with per-route batch size, batching window, prefix cache window, KV prefetch enablement, and allowlist/denylist flags.
- Safety: dry-run simulator, telemetry-driven rollback triggers (error rate, latency, token cost delta), canary percentages, manual override.

Approach:
1) Policy compiler: rule engine that materializes high-level segment definitions into numeric runtime knobs. Keep output schema compact, versioned, and signed.
2) Recommendation engine: telemetry-backed heuristics + small offline optimizer that suggests knobs per tenant-route pair. Initially conservative defaults, then progressive amplification for low-risk cohorts.
3) Safe apply: config deployment orchestration with staged canary, metric monitors in Console, and automatic rollback if thresholds cross.
4) Simulation & verification: run synthetic load against a sandbox runtime using historical traces (dry-run) and generate report with projected cost and latency deltas.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Conservative vs aggressive batching: start conservative for non-deterministic routes (LLM tool-calling, structured outputs) to avoid regressions.
- Per-tenant vs per-route granularity: prefer per-tenant+per-route composite keys for compactness; full per-connection tuning reserved for high-tier customers.
- Allowlist/denylist precedence: explicit denylist overrides allowlist and auto-recommendations; RBAC-protected admin overrides.

Security & compliance: policy bundles are stored encrypted at rest and signed; audit logs recorded to customer-specific audit streams for Private deployments. KMS integration required for sign/verify operations.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Week 0: merge compiler core and simulator (PR 1234).
- Week 1: run dry-run across 5 representative tenant cohorts in sandbox and verify telemetry.
- Week 2: 1% canary on hosted runtime for P95 sensitive routes; monitor for 72h.
- Week 3: expand to 10% and gating to 25% with automated rollback policy.

Deliverables: policy compiler binary, recommendation job, dry-run harness, Console dashboard panels for canary health, rollout orchestration playbook, and runbook for manual remediation.
